 Mr. S.S. Chaudhary, Standing
Counsel, for the State.
(2) Since the issue involved in both the
writ petitions is identical, therefore, these are
being heard and decided together by this
com mon judgm ent. However, for brevity, facts
of Writ Petition (S/ S) No. 1718 of 2021 alone
are being considered and discussed here, in
which petitioners have sought the following
reliefs:
 "I . To issue writ, order or direction in
the nature of m andam us comm anding the
respondents to grant without any delay with
im m ediate effect, the benefit of tim e scale
after com puting their 10 years of service from
the date of their initial appointm ent and
release the benefit without any delay within a
period as stipulated by this Hon'ble Court.
 I I . To issue writ, order or direction in
the nature of m andam us directing the
respondents to grant the pensionary benefit as
per the old Pension Scheme, which was in
force at the tim e of petitioner's initial
appointment in the Nav Deep Public Junior
High School Sailkhula, Deval, District
Cham oli."
(3) Learned Counsel for the petitioners,
on instructions, submits that he is not pressing
prayer no. I I and confining the relief to prayer
no. I alone.
(4) According to petitioners, they were
appointed in a privately m anaged unaided
recognised school on different dates and the
school in which they were so appointed was
thereafter included in the grant-in-aid list.

2026:UHC:3998
Petitioners were granted benefit of selection
grade and promotional pay scale in term s of
the governm ent policy after taking into
account the services rendered by them in
aided school. Petitioners contend that services
rendered by them before inclusion of the
school concerned in grant-in-aid list also need
to be taken into account for grant of m onetary
benefits.
(5) Learned State Counsel submits that
petitioners have sought a writ of m andam us,
but no representation has been m ade by them
staking claim for such relief, therefore writ
petition is not m aintainable. Learned Counsel
for the petitioners, however, submits that
petitioners have repeatedly represented the
m atter before the authorities concerned,
although representations so made have not
been enclosed with the writ petition.
(6) Be that as it may, since petitioners
have sought a writ of m andamus, therefore,
without expressing any opinion on the m erits
of the claim staked by petitioners, writ
petitions are disposed of by permitting
petitioners to m ake their separate
representation before the com petent authority.
I f petitioners m ake such representation staking
claim for aforesaid monetary benefits within
two weeks from today, decision thereupon
shall be taken by Chief Education Officer
concerned, as per law, within four m onths
thereafter.
 ( Man oj Ku m ar Tiw ar i, J.)
